assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Distance
items.clue: The total length of the path travelled by a body.

items.label: Terminal speed
items.clue: The constant value eventually reached by a body falling through a fluid.

items.label: Acceleration of free fall, g
items.clue: The acceleration of a body moving under gravity alone, with no fluid resistance.

questions.stem: A body moves from point P to point Q. Which statement about its displacement is correct?

options.text: Its magnitude can be less than the distance travelled, but never greater.
It equals the total length of the path followed from P to Q.
It depends on the route taken, whereas the distance does not.
It is always positive, because it is a length measured in metres.

questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change in position from P to Q; distance is the length of the path. The straight line is the shortest route, so the magnitude of the displacement equals the distance only for one-way motion along a straight line and is otherwise smaller.

questions.stem: A car travels 3.0 km along a straight road at a constant speed of 10 m s⁻¹, then returns along the same road to its starting point at a constant speed of 15 m s⁻¹. What are its average speed and its average velocity for the whole journey?

options.text: Average speed 12.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity 12 m s⁻¹
Average speed 12 m s⁻¹; average velocity −2.5 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: The outward leg takes 300 s and the return leg 200 s, so average speed = 6000 m ÷ 500 s = 12 m s⁻¹. The car finishes where it started, so its displacement is zero and so is its average velocity.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 16 m s⁻¹ brakes with uniform deceleration and comes to rest in 4.0 s. What distance does the car travel while braking?
questions.explanation: With uniform acceleration, s = ((u + v)/2)t = ((16 + 0)/2) × 4.0 = 32 m. The same answer follows from s = ut + ½at² with a = −4.0 m s⁻²: 64 − 32 = 32 m.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a point 1.20 m above the ground. It rises to a maximum height of 6.70 m above the ground, falls, and is caught at a point 1.70 m above the ground. Upwards is taken as positive. What are the distance travelled by the ball and its displacement, from the throw to the catch?
questions.explanation: Distance is the length of the path: 5.50 m up then 5.00 m down, 10.5 m in total. Displacement is the change in position, final minus initial: 1.70 m − 1.20 m = +0.50 m, upwards.

questions.stem: A car starts from rest at t = 0 and x = 0 and moves along a straight road. A graph of its position x against time t is a curve that gets steeper with time. At t = 3.0 s, x = 16.5 m, and the tangent to the curve at this point also passes through the point (5.0 s, 40.5 m). What is the instantaneous velocity of the car at t = 3.0 s?
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the gradient of the tangent to the position–time graph: (40.5 − 16.5) m ÷ (5.0 − 3.0) s = 24 m ÷ 2.0 s = 12 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A stone is released from rest and falls 5.00 m. Fluid resistance is negligible. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the speed of the stone when it has fallen 5.00 m?
questions.explanation: With downwards positive, v² = u² + 2as = 0 + 2 × 9.8 × 5.00 = 98.0 m² s⁻², so v = √98.0 = 9.90 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: Which statement about when the equations of motion s = ((u + v)/2)t, v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² and v² = u² + 2as can be applied is correct?

options.text: They apply to any straight-line motion, even if the acceleration varies.
They apply to a skydiver falling through air, as g is constant.
They apply whenever the acceleration is constant in size and direction.
They apply only until the body stops and reverses its direction.

questions.explanation: The equations are derived by assuming constant acceleration, and that is the only condition. They then apply to the whole motion, including through an instant of zero velocity, provided one sign convention is used.
